Anon
a-NON
adverb
From Old English on ān, “into one, in one (moment)” — that is, at once; an adverb meaning “straightway, immediately, presently.”

Biblical Definition

Anon means “straightway, at once, immediately,” born of the Old English phrase “in one moment.” It stands twice in the KJV, and in both places it marks a swift response — but the two could not be more different in what they teach. In the parable of the sower, the stony-ground hearer “heareth the word, and anon with joy receiveth it” (Mat 13:20); the very speed is the flaw. His quick, glad reception has no root, and “dureth for a while,” so that “when tribulation or persecution ariseth… by and by he is offended” (Mat 13:21). Anon received, anon offended: shallow soil warms fast and dries fast, and the emotion that leaps up in a moment withers in a moment. Against this stands the “anon” of true and needful haste: “Simon’s wife’s mother lay sick of a fever, and anon they tell him of her” (Mar 1:30), and the Lord straightway heals her, and she straightway ministers (Mar 1:31). Here quickness is faith — bringing the need at once to Christ, and rising at once to serve. So the word sets two speeds side by side: the hasty joy that has no root, and the ready faith that runs to Jesus with its trouble. The question is never merely whether a man responds anon, but what abides when the first quickness is spent — whether there was root beneath the leaf.

Webster 1828 Definition

“Straightway, immediately” — contrasting the rootless haste of the stony hearer with the ready faith that runs to Christ.

ANON, straightway; immediately; at once; presently.

From Old English on ān, “in one (moment).”

The stony hearer “anon with joy receiveth” the word (Mat 13:20).

That quickness has no root and withers in trouble (Mat 13:21).

“Anon they tell him” of the fever — haste of faith (Mar 1:30).

Key Scripture

Mat 13:20 — "But he that received the seed into stony places, the same is he that heareth the word, and anon with joy receiveth it;"

Mar 1:30 — "But Simon's wife's mother lay sick of a fever, and anon they tell him of her."

Mat 13:21 — "Yet hath he not root in himself, but dureth for a while: for when tribulation or persecution ariseth because of the word, by and by he is offended."

Mar 1:31 — "And he came and took her by the hand, and lifted her up; and immediately the fever left her, and she ministered unto them."

Modern Corruption

Not a doctrine under dispute but a lost word for “at once”; it recovers the warning that quick joy without root is no saving faith.

expand to see more

The word rebukes the shallow religion of the sudden. The stony hearer receives anon, with joy, and the age applauds exactly such quick warm responses — the instant decision, the emotional high, the fast profession. But anon received is anon offended; soil that warms fast dries fast, and the man who had no root endures only for a while. Christ Himself teaches us to distrust a joy that has not been tested by tribulation. What comes up in a night can wither in a day.

This entry faces no significant postmodern redefinition. The principle to recover is rootedness — that the worth of a response is proved not by its speed but by what abides when trouble comes. There is a good “anon,” the haste of faith that runs at once to Christ with its trouble and rises at once to serve Him (Mar 1:30-31); and there is a deadly one, the quick joy without depth of earth. Let the reader see that he be rooted and grounded (Eph 3:17), lest he be a hearer only, and anon offended.

Greek & Hebrew Roots

From Old English on ān, “in one moment,” “anon” means “straightway” — the speed that saves or the speed that shames.

expand to see more

Anon — Old English on ān, “into one moment”; at once.

It means straightway, immediately, presently.

The stony hearer anon receives the word with joy (Mat 13:20).

Lacking root, he dureth for a while and is offended (Mat 13:21).

“Anon they tell him” — the good haste of faith (Mar 1:30).

Usage

"Anon received, anon offended: quick joy withered in the heat."

"There is a haste of faith that runs at once to Christ with its need."

"Ask not only whether a man responds anon, but what abides after."
